thread:
maria: Heads-up — ACME (customer-prod-usw2) reports a sudden p99 latency regression on text-gen endpoints starting ~03:10 UTC. p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~750ms, p99 from ~300ms -> ~2.5s. Errors are timeouts at 10s for some requests.

jason: Any deploys/infra changes around that window?

maria: Yes — we pushed host kernel security patch to 20% of nodes at 02:40, then CUDA driver 525.60.13 rolled to dedicated pools at 02:52. GPU firmware v1.3.2 rollout finished around 03:00 (small batch).

dena: Are storage metrics noisy? NVMe contention can show exactly like this.

maria: Attaching the short iostat snapshot from an affected host:

```
Device            tps    MB_read/s    MB_wrtn/s    await
nvme0n1         1200        30.4         12.2      185.7
nvme1n1          560        10.1          5.8      142.3
```

maria: Not ideal — high await and tps correlated to the spikes in the request traces. KV-cache miss rate also higher than baseline.

rob: Looks like host IO tail. Two hypotheses: 1) kernel patch changed block/qdisc default, exposing NVMe scheduling regressions; 2) CUDA/driver/firmware increased host-side housekeeping leading to IO storms.

eli: We should repro with a synthetic load hitting the same model/seq len distribution and disabling prefix caching to amplify reads. I can run a canary in eu1.

jason: For immediate mitigation — suggested order: 1) enable fallback routing to smaller model (keeps latencies down), 2) throttle background maintenance (snapshot/defrag) on affected hosts, 3) remove nodes from routing that have both kernel+driver rolled. Can we do 1 now?

maria: Enabled fallback routing for ACME (model-route fallback -> rtx-small) at 03:22 UTC. Customer traffic shifted, tail improved but still above SLO in some bursts.

oncall: Incident created: INC-2026-4598765432 (link: https://incident.redwood/INC-4598765432) — paging oncall.

rob: While eli repros, let's plan a quick rollback test: pick 3 hosts, revert kernel patch only (leave driver/firmware) and run the same synthetic. If tail drops, kernel likely the trigger. If not, try driver rollback.

eli: Repro started on canary (eu1-cpu1) @03:35 with 200 rps, seq len 512, prefix cache off. I'll post traces after run.

maria: Also toggled I/O cgroup throttling for batch jobs on the affected host pool (throttle -> 30% bw) to reduce interference.

jason: Any quick kernel boot flags we can try instead of full rollback? Maybe disable blk-mq or set elevator to none temporarily? Risky but faster.

rob: We can try toggling vm.swappiness and blk-mq off on one host for a fast test. Schedule a rollback if that doesn't help.

eli: Canary results: p95 ~200ms, p99 ~1.1s on rollback-host (kernel reverted). On hosts with kernel patch still present p99 ~2.4s. So rollback reduces tail by ~55%.

maria: Good repro. Rolling kernel rollback to all affected pool nodes (batch of 10) starting 03:58 UTC. Will monitor for regressions.

oncall: Rolling back kernel on nodes: host-23, host-27, host-31... (progress updates coming).

dena: Post-rollback quick mitigations to add to runbook: - pin NVMe power management off for affected SKUs - enable per-tenant burst limits - tune blk-mq/queue_depth for NVMe - keep kv-cache warm during rollouts

rob: Long term action items: 1) Add kernel-driver compatibility test to preflight (block-level IO workload with GPUs running housekeeping) 2) Add monitoring for NVMe await per model-route 3) Add automated canary rollback when p99 > threshold during infra rollouts.

maria: Owners/ETAs: eli -> finish node rollbacks + post-checks by 04:15 UTC; dena -> update runbook + doc by EOD; rob -> create follow-up task for preflight tests (JIRA INFRA-1289).

jason: Customer notified via support at 03:50 — they confirmed improved experience after fallback + rollbacks, asked for RCA and ETA.

maria: Current status @04:05 UTC: rollbacks complete on primary affected pool, p95 ~140ms, p99 ~380ms (close to baseline), continuing monitoring for 2h.

eli: Will attach perf traces and iostat dumps to the incident ticket in 15m.

sre-bot: Postmortem template created and assigned to dena. Reminder: include exact kernel/driver/firmware versions and timeline.

rob: Thanks team. Follow-ups in INC-2026-4598765432.
